skills.name: Trigonometric ratios of 30°, 45° and 60°; using a calculator

note.text:
Exact values to learn:
• sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, tan 30° = 1/√3
• sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2 (= √2/2), tan 45° = 1
• sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3
They come from half an equilateral triangle (30°, 60°) and half a square (45°).
Calculator: check it is in degree mode (D or DEG). sin 37° ≈ 0.6018. To find an angle from a ratio use the inverse key: sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°.

sections.heading: Where the exact values come from
sections.text:
Half of a square with side {1}: the angles are {45}°, {45}° and {90}°; the diagonal is √{2}. So sin {45}° = cos {45}° = {1} ÷ √{2} and tan {45}° = {1}.
Half of an equilateral triangle with side {2}: the angles are {30}°, {60}° and {90}°; the sides are {1}, √{3} and {2}. So:
• sin {30}° = {frac(1, 2)}, cos {30}° = √{3} ÷ {2}, tan {30}° = {1} ÷ √{3}
• sin {60}° = √{3} ÷ {2}, cos {60}° = {frac(1, 2)}, tan {60}° = √{3}.

sections.heading: Using a calculator
sections.text:
First check the calculator shows D or DEG (degree mode). In radian mode every answer is wrong.
To find sin {37}°, press sin {37} = and read about {roundTo(sinD(37), 0.0001)}.
To find an angle from a ratio, use the inverse: SHIFT then sin gives sin⁻¹. If sin θ = {0.5}, then θ = sin⁻¹({0.5}) = {30}°.
Keep four decimal places while working; round only the final answer.

sections.heading: Angles of elevation
sections.text:
Look up at the top of a tree: the angle between the level ground and your line of sight is the angle of elevation. Looking down from a cliff gives an angle of depression.
If you stand {20} m from a tree and the elevation is {35}°, the height h satisfies tan {35}° = h ÷ {20}, so h = {20} × tan {35}° ≈ {roundTo(20 * tanD(35), 0.1)} m.

key_words.meaning: a value written with fractions and roots, not rounded
the calculator setting for angles in degrees
sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹: from a ratio back to the angle
the angle looking up from the horizontal

mistake.why: That value comes from radian mode. Set the calculator to degrees (DEG).

worked_example.problem: From a point {d} m from the foot of a tree, the angle of elevation of the top is {A}°. Find the height of the tree to {1} decimal place.

cards.idea: Learn the exact values for {30}°, {45}° and {60}°.
Use a calculator in degree mode; round as the question asks.
The inverse key gives the angle: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹.

check.prompt: {R} θ = {r}. Find the acute angle θ to {1} decimal place.

misconceptions.explain: {R}⁻¹ is the inverse function (the angle), not {1} ÷ {r}.

pick.y: In half a square, opposite = adjacent, so tan 45° = 1.

questions.prompt: What is the exact value of {X.q}?
Use a calculator: find {R} {A}° to {4} decimal places.

misconceptions.explain: Check you pressed the right key: {R}, not {R == 'sin' ? 'cos' : 'sin'}.

questions.prompt: {R} θ = {r}. Find the acute angle θ to {1} decimal place.

misconceptions.explain: {R}⁻¹ is the inverse function (the angle), not {1} ÷ {r}.

questions.prompt: Without a calculator, find the value of {X.e}.
From a point {d} m from the foot of a tree on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the tree is {A}°. Find the height of the tree to {1} decimal place.

misconceptions.explain: The distance {d} m is adjacent to the angle and the height is opposite: use tan.
